title: POC TTFT vs TPOT tradeoff and fallback playbook - Artemis Fleet
summary: Discovery + POC scoping to define latency SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT), p95/p99 targets, fallback policies, and a concrete measurement plan. Customer requires on-prem-like guarantees and detailed audit trail for trial. Agreement to run a staged benchmark: synthetic traffic, production replay subset, and an A/B fallback test across model variants.
topics: Define TTFT vs TPOT acceptance criteria
action_items: Diego Ramos | Build bench harness for TTFT and TPOT sweep (1qps, 10qps, 100qps, 1k qps) and include KV cache hot/warm scenarios | 2027-07-27
Alex Morgan | Provide production sampling window and representative prompt set (50-200 tokens typical) | 2027-07-23
Grace Ho | Share compliance checklist (SOC2 scope and KMS requirements) and confirm allowed data flows | 2027-07-26
Maya Chen | Share Redwood measurement playbook doc + sample synthetic traffic scripts | 2027-07-21
next_steps: Redwood to run initial synthetic benchmark in Redwood Dedicated sandbox next Tue/Thu
Customer to provision test VPC endpoint and share access logs for replay
Schedule 90-minute benchmark run and debrief after results
Exchange PS estimate for 2-week POC with 24/7 SE on-call
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-20
Time: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Redwood CSM); Alex Morgan (Artemis Head of ML), Priya Singh (Infra), Tom Diaz (SRE), Evan Li (Product), Grace Ho (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy): Agree to TTFT and TPOT benchmarks plus fallback policy. Need synthetic + replay tests; security gating for pilot.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about an hour, want to make sure we come out with a clear SLO definition, the measurement plan, and next steps. Quick intros?
[00:12] Alex Morgan (Artemis): Alex here, I run the ML org. We're evaluating Redwood for inference for fleet dispatch chatbots, mainly latency-sensitive prompts, and some bulk batch scoring.
[00:20] Priya Singh (Infra): Priya, infra lead. Our constraints are 1) VPC only traffic, 2) audit logs, 3) bursty QPS during shift changes.
[00:28] Diego Ramos (Redwood SE): Diego - I'll own the bench and the SLO plumbing. Quick note: we'll look at both TTFT — time to first token — and TPOT — total per output token — since you have short confirmation messages and also longer route summaries.
[00:38] Tom Diaz (SRE): Tom — on-call. We care about p95 for user-facing confirmations and p99 for automated safety checks.

[00:52] Maya: Great. High-level ask from Artemis? What does success look like for the POC?
[00:58] Evan Li (Product): For the POC we need three things: 1) demonstrate tail latency under realistic load, 2) verify cost / throughput tradeoff at 500 qps steady with 1k brief bursts, 3) validated fallback so dispatch doesn't fail.
[01:10] Alex: Add an audit trail for every inference, and we need to see p99 under 700ms for short outputs (~16 tokens).
[01:18] Grace Ho (Security): And SOC2 scope — no customer PII leaves the VPC, KMS for keys. We'll need logs and proof that data-at-rest encryption is in place during the trial.

[01:30] Diego: Noted. On the measurement side, we propose three stages: 1) synthetic microbench (single client, controlled inputs) to profile baseline TTFT/TPOT per model variant; 2) scaled synthetic (traffic shaping across qps buckets to model bursts); 3) production replay (sampled traces) to validate real-world behavior. Does that align?
[01:46] Priya: Yes but we need to know sample size for replay and how you warm caches — K-B cache warmup? (laugh)
[01:53] Diego: (laugh) K-B cache, yeah. We'll include KV cache warm and cold scenarios. For sample size, we recommend 10k requests for p95 stable estimate and 50k for p99 in heavy-tailed workloads, but we can start smaller and bootstrap.
[02:08] Tom: 50k seems high but acceptable if we spread it over windows; need to ensure no production impact.
[02:14] Maya: We'll orchestrate replay against isolated test endpoint; no writes to your production.

[02:22] Alex: For SLO targets — we discussed p99 700ms for short outputs. For longer outputs (200 tokens) what's reasonable?
[02:30] Diego: For long outputs, TTFT matters less: we suggest p95 TPOT under 2.2s at 200 tokens on our quantized medium model. But we'll show full curve vs model variant.
[02:39] Evan: Can you map TTFT to user experience? Our product team cares about how first token latency affects perceived responsiveness.
[02:45] Diego: Sure — TTFT is the initial acknowledgment; for confirmations we target TTFT p95 < 120ms ideally, p99 < 250ms if possible. For longer completions, TPOT per 10 tokens metric might be clearer: e.g., average 120ms per 10 tokens on quantized path.

[03:05] Grace: What about fallbacks? We can't afford total unavailability. We need automatic model-variant fallback and cross-region failover.
[03:12] Maya: Redwood supports routing policies; we'll define a fallback playbook: primary -> lower-cost degenerate model (faster, lower accuracy) -> regional fallback -> queued-backoff with degraded UX. We'll demo canary traffic and A/B routing so you can measure impact.
[03:29] Priya: Okay, but how do you measure the UX impact quantitatively?
[03:34] Diego: We'll instrument synthetic user flows with weighted metrics: success rate, response time buckets, and a quality proxy (n-gram similarity against golden answers for the sampled prompt set). We'll include delta in quality when falling back.
[03:46] Alex: That proxy might be noisy. We'll accept it for now as a coarse indicator. The POC acceptance should include a manual QA review on a handful of prompts.
[03:55] Maya: Noted — include 200 QA checks across categories.

[04:02] Evan: Timeline — how long to stand up the benchmark and get results?
[04:06] Diego: If we get prompts and sample windows this week, we can run bench script and a first synthetic pass in 4 business days. Replay will take longer because of data handoff, maybe 10 business days total to full report.
[04:18] Alex: We need results before the end of month to make a decision. Is that feasible?
[04:22] Maya: Yes, we'll prioritize. We'll propose bookings for bench slots and SE on-call.

[04:30] Tom: One technical question — how are you handling KV cache hits in your measurements? We need to understand warm vs cold cache behavior because our bursts are often repeating queries.
[04:38] Diego: We'll run three cache profiles: cold (no prior rows), warm (single client reuse), and hot (global prefix reuse). We'll show per-token cost and latency breakdown including cache hit rate. Note: logs may show "cache miss" spelled weird in our auto transcriptions but we'll provide clean metrics.
[04:54] Priya: Also need to know what obs data you'll share — token-level latencies, request IDs, model version.
[05:00] Nina (Redwood CSM): We'll provide token-level breakdowns, request traces, and rollup dashboards with p50/p95/p99 and percentiles. Can share CSV exports for your analytics.
[05:10] Grace: On encryption and audit — we need to vet your key handling and confirm HSM/KMS integration.
[05:14] Maya: We'll send our security pack and a checklist. If needed, we can arrange a short technical security call with our compliance lead.
[05:22] Alex: For acceptance criteria, let's put it down explicitly so no ambiguity: 1) TTFT p95 < 120ms and p99 < 250ms for short confirmations (<=16 tokens) under 500 qps steady-state; 2) TPOT p95 < 2.2s for 200-token summaries at 500 qps steady with 1k qps 1-minute bursts; 3) Fallback must trigger with measurable quality delta < 10% on our QA proxy and maintain availability > 99.9% during induced failures.
[05:45] Diego: We can map instrumentation to each criteria and produce an acceptance matrix.
[05:50] Evan: Can we see cost delta per million tokens between variants?
[05:53] Maya: Yes we'll include unit economics — tokens per second, GPU-hours estimates, and projected monthly cost for your traffic profile.
[06:00] Alex: Great. Any legal/procurement blockers now?
[06:03] Grace: We'll need a short NDA addendum for telemetry sharing and a SOC2 attestation before full pilot.
[06:09] Maya: We'll start the docs flow.
[06:13] Nina: I'll follow up with calendar invites for bench slots and a doc with the measurement playbook link.
[06:20] Maya: Anything else?
[06:22] Tom: One last thing — alerting thresholds. We'll want runbook triggers for p99 > 700ms or error rate increase > 0.5%.
[06:29] Diego: We'll add recommended alerting thresholds and a suggested runbook for mitigation.
[06:34] Alex: Perfect. Thanks everyone.
[06:36] Maya: Recap — Diego builds bench harness, Alex provides prompts and sample windows, Grace provides security checklist, Redwood runs synthetic bench, schedule replay once infra is ready. We'll reconvene after the first benchmark.
[06:46] Evan: Thanks — talk soon.
[06:50] (call ends)
notes: Transcript contains typical ASR issues (names/acronyms occasionally garbled) and filler words. Audio quality medium. References: Redwood bench harness repo (link shared post-call), measurement playbook doc, security pack (to be shared).
